podcast-dannyjones-JKLKxQKcvtw:
Two brothers who research ancient sites join Danny Jones for this episode. Known to their audience as the Snake Bros, they argue that Gobekli Tepe in Turkey is not what the public has been told. They make the same case for Easter Island in the Pacific. They present new evidence, as they frame it, for older dates, buried structures, and purposes the standard accounts miss.

Gobekli Tepe already rewrote prehistory once, pushing monumental building back thousands of years; the brothers argue the revision has further to go. Jones follows their site reports and asks what would settle the questions. Archaeologists urge caution about the brothers' readings, and the claims remain theirs. The episode preserves the tour-guide version of a live debate: two field enthusiasts making the case that the oldest places on earth still hide their main chapters underground.
podcast-dannyjones-272W-JxGFtw:
Comedian AJ Wilkerson talks with Danny Jones about life after an autism diagnosis. Wilkerson began stand-up about two years after learning he was autistic. He tours in a battered van he loves.

He tells Jones how the van became his rolling home and office. He explains signs that led him to seek answers about himself. The title promises a guide to knowing if you share his condition. Wilkerson mixes jokes with plain talk, so the episode works as both a comic visit and a candid first-person account. His honesty gives the laughs real heart.
podcast-joerogan-6jdaXp0iwtw:
Professor Gad Saad joins Joe Rogan for episode 2497. Saad studies how evolution shapes consumer and social behavior. His book The Parasitic Mind attacks bad ideas as mental parasites.

Rogan asks how weak ideas spread through schools and media. Saad defends reason, science, and free speech in blunt terms. Fans call him the Gadfather for his bold style. The talk ranges over campus life and public debate. It suits listeners who like their cultural criticism served with data, jokes, and no fear of giving offense. His wit keeps the big claims grounded and fun.
